name: RuView
description: π RuView turns commodity WiFi signals into real-time spatial intelligence, vital sign monitoring, and presence detection — all without a single pixel of video.
one_liner: Turns an ordinary WiFi router into a sensor that can tell whether someone is home, how they're breathing, and whether they've fallen — using only radio signals and no cameras at all.
buyer: An operator of an assisted-living or elder-care facility who needs fall and vital-sign monitoring for residents but can't install cameras for privacy and dignity reasons.
business_use_cases: An elder-care facility deploys cheap sensor nodes in each room to get fall detection and breathing/heart-rate alerts without any camera, satisfying residents' privacy concerns.
A smart-home installer adds camera-free presence and room-occupancy sensing to security systems for privacy-conscious homeowners, integrating with Home Assistant or Apple Home.
A hotel or coworking operator uses the room-occupancy and activity signals to automate cleaning schedules and space utilization reporting without installing cameras.

money_ideas.idea: Sell pre-configured ESP32 sensor kits bundled with a monthly monitoring/alerting subscription to families with elderly relatives at home.
Offer installation and integration services for smart-home installers wanting to add camera-free sensing to existing Home Assistant setups.

steal_this: Buy a couple of cheap ESP32 boards this weekend, wire up the Home Assistant integration in one room, and pitch a local assisted-living facility a free pilot in exchange for a case study.
